To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we present a theoretical model for optimizing iterative crowdsourced workflows based on POMDMs; 2) we propose a system to learn TURKONTOL’s POMDP model parameters from real MechanicalTurk data; 3) our system applies the model to control live tasks on Mechanical Turk, producing superior artifacts; and 4) our system learns the model parameters in real-time, and adapts to changes in the task, worker population, and task quality.

(a) we present an end-to-end framework for learning and using TURKONTROLPOMDPs to improve crowd-sourced workflows and (b) we demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework by showing significant improvements in artifact quality over existing nonadaptive methods.
we have designed a novel POMDP model that is able to learn from noisy data and that we can apply the model to optimize a real-world crowd-sourcing task.
